title: Closed base change for integral direct images of lisse continuous modules
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its norm topology, and an algebraic closure $\Omega\supset E$ with its extended norm topology. For $F=E$ or $\Omega$, let $C_F(Q)=C(Q,F)$ on all profinite sets, using all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and put $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Work with internal modules, ordinary unbounded derived categories and K-injective total right derived direct images on small pro-etale sites [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Lisse means pro-etale locally finite free [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. All sites, parameter sets and resolutions lie in compatible coefficient universes.

Let $q:X\to U$ be an integral morphism of affine $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let $s:Z\hookrightarrow U$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $X_Z=X\times_U Z$, with $h:X_Z\to X$ and $q_Z:X_Z\to Z$. For a finite-rank lisse $C_{F,X}$-module $\mathcal L$, the canonical derived exchange is an isomorphism
$$\beta_{q,s,\mathcal L}:s^*Rq_*(\mathcal L[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}R(q_Z)_*(h^*\mathcal L[0]).$$
The map is the adjunct under $q_Z^*\dashv R(q_Z)_*$ of $q_Z^*s^*Rq_*\mathcal L\cong h^*q^*Rq_*\mathcal L\xrightarrow{h^*\varepsilon}\,h^*\mathcal L$, with the canonical coefficient and pullback-composition identifications. It is natural in maps of lisse modules, in isomorphisms of the cartesian square, and in pro-etale base change of $U$; these naturalities also hold after any further profinite parametrization $U[Q]\to U$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. For an $E$-module and its ordinary scalar extension to $\Omega$, these exchange maps commute, after scalar restriction, with the actual map $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. No exactness of $q_*$ on arbitrary pro-etale sheaves and no scalar-extension/direct-image isomorphism is asserted.

proof.text: Set $\Lambda=C_F$. Cover the affine ind-etale basis of $Z$ by affine ind-etale objects $V=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C$ whose rings are w-contractible: apply [sk-thm-pe-wc-cover] to the coordinate ring of each basis object and compose the ind-etale maps, using [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. This suffices to detect isomorphisms of cohomology sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. The lift $W=v(V)=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties] satisfies $W\times_U Z=V$; [lem-zl-henselian-indetale-closed-lift] makes $(C,IC)$ henselian. By [lem-zl-condensed-henselian-lisse-rigidity], $W$ is w-contractible because $V$ is. Thus these are admissible tests for [lem-sfb-closed-test-derived-exchange-model].

source.place: Corollary 4.4(2); closed lifts: Bhatt–Scholze Lemmas 6.1.1–6.1.2, and Stacks 09BK

proof.text: Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and $D=B\otimes_A C$. Then $T=X\times_UW=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $T_0=X\times_UV=\operatorname{Spec}(D/ID)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change], $D$ is integral over $C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-over-henselian-pair] to the henselian pair $(C,IC)$ of step 1 and this integral algebra: $(D,(IC)D)=(D,ID)$ is henselian. The closed immersion in these coordinates is $a:T_0\hookrightarrow T$.

source.place: Tag 09XK, lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair; base change of integrality is algebra.tex Tag 02JK, lemma-base-change-integral (1).

proof.text: The affine scheme $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite] to the quasi-coherent algebra associated to the integral $C$-algebra $D$. It gives a small directed system of finite, finitely presented quasi-coherent algebras on $W$ with colimit the algebra associated to $D$. Evaluating on the affine $W$ gives $C$-algebras $D_i$ finite as $C$-modules and finitely presented as $C$-algebras, and $D=\varinjlim_i D_i$: evaluation of this colimit is the ring colimit by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-colimit]. The directed index is nonempty, and its transition maps are unital $C$-algebra maps; they need not be injective. Since $C$ is w-contractible by step 1, [lem-sfb-indfinite-contractible-base-wstrict] applies and makes $D$ w-strictly local. This uses finite presentation of the approximating algebras, not finite presentation of $D/C$, and makes no w-contractibility claim about $D$.

source.place: Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite (2), specialized to the affine base; combined with lem-sfb-indfinite-contractible-base-wstrict (Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.1.9 and Example 2.2.2; finite-stage Stacks Tag 0986).

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-henselian-wstrict-local-invariance] to the henselian pair $(D,ID)$: since $D$ is w-strictly local, so is $D/ID$. Independently, the first clause of [lem-zl-condensed-henselian-lisse-rigidity] gives that the actual map $\pi_0(a):\pi_0(T_0)\to\pi_0(T)$ is a homeomorphism; this clause needs only henselianity, so no w-contractibility of $T$ is required. Put $M=\mathcal L|_T$. Pulling a pro-etale finite-free trivializing cover and its finite bases back along $T\to X$ proves that $M$ is finite-rank lisse, in precisely the sense of [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. The coefficient ring is still the pulled-back commutative condensed ring $C_F$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring].

source.place: Corollary 4.4(1) for the component homeomorphism, and Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.2.13 for henselian weak strict locality.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-wstrict-lisse-component-cohomology] with $h=a:T_0\to T$, $\Lambda=C_F$ and the lisse module $M$. Both schemes are affine and w-strictly local, and $\pi_0(a)$ is a homeomorphism by steps 3–4. The theorem says exactly that the canonical restriction $R\Gamma(T,M[0])\to R\Gamma(T_0,a^*M[0])$ induced by the actual adjunction unit is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. Its arbitrary-condensed-ring hypothesis applies to all continuous $\Omega$-valued functions with the extended norm topology. Thus no completeness or finite-subextension replacement of coefficients is used. This is the derived restriction appearing in [lem-sfb-closed-test-derived-exchange-model].

source.place: Lemma 4.1, Proposition 4.3, equation (4.2), and Corollary 4.7, through the existing agent-formulated w-strictly local extension lem-sfb-wstrict-lisse-component-cohomology.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-closed-test-derived-exchange-model], the map just proved invertible is $R\Gamma(V,\beta_{q,s,\mathcal L})$. On every chosen $V$, evaluation is exact [lem-zl-contractible-derived-sections-tensor], so the cone of $\beta$ has zero evaluated cohomology. These tests cover the affine ind-etale basis; hence each cohomology sheaf of that cone vanishes by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. The cone is acyclic, proving that the specified derived mate $\beta$ is an isomorphism. The test-model lemma identifies the arrow, not just its source and target. All complexes started in degree zero and all derived direct images of these modules are bounded below; the conclusion is their isomorphism in the ordinary unbounded derived category.

source.place: Derived closed-test model and exact contractible evaluation; ordinary bounded-below computations embedded in the unbounded derived category

proof.text: The naturality in $\mathcal L$, square isomorphisms and pro-etale base change is the naturality of the derived restriction in [lem-sfb-closed-test-derived-exchange-model]. The model uses the canonical adjunction and composition identifications, so it gives equalities for the specified mate independently of the test choices used to prove invertibility. A profinite parameter $Q$ gives a pro-etale object $U[Q]\to U$ by [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]; the same naturality applies on that entire object, not just after evaluation at points of $Q$. For $E\to\Omega$, ordinary scalar extension of a locally finite free module is locally finite free, by applying the tensor relation to a finite basis. Apply the coefficient-map clause of the test-model lemma to the actual section map $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. On each test its two composites are the same restriction of $1\otimes x$; the derived comparison clause gives equality of the derived morphisms after scalar restriction. The comparison maps in that square are the canonical right-derived coefficient comparisons; their invertibility is not needed. This proves precisely the scalar compatibility asserted in the item.

source.place: Naturality of derived restriction and coefficient-map clause of the closed-test model

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NB-817f9f5cc (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Re-delivery after the C5 RETURN of 5fc3874d; all requested repairs are done. The item's statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint fields are byte-identical to the returned head; only proof, proof_deps and split_report changed. (a) The integral-locality node is dropped. Step 3 uses clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite (0817) on the affine, hence qcqs, Spec C. Evaluating on Spec C with the quasi-coherent-algebra-colimit node gives finite, finitely presented D_i with colimit D, and lem-sfb-indfinite-contractible-base-wstrict then makes D w-strictly local. (b) The hypercover node is dropped. lem-zl-henselian-wstrict-local-invariance applied to the henselian pair (D,ID) makes D/ID w-strictly local. The rigidity node's unconditional first clause gives the pi_0 homeomorphism. lem-sfb-wstrict-lisse-component-cohomology then gives the unit-induced restriction RΓ(T,L|_T)→RΓ(T_0,a^*L|_T) as an isomorphism for any condensed Λ, so the all-continuous Ω coefficients are kept. (c) The hypercover clause and the det-pe-hypercover-complex dependency were removed from lem-sfb-closed-test-derived-exchange-model. (d) The kept node is true: by Stacks 09BL(2) (proetale.tex lemma-closed-immersion-affines-apply), with K-injective restriction to slices and transposition of h^*ε. It identifies the arrow, assumes neither integrality nor lisseness, and asserts no invertibility, so it is not a restatement of the item (D1). A search of all chapters found only underived pbc closed-immersion nodes. Coordinate-face proves a special case inline in its step 6 and has no node, so this is not a C5 duplicate. Steps 1, 2, 6 and 7 were checked against the cited statements: the henselian closed lift, w-contractibility of the lift, integrality and henselian base change, exact evaluation plus conservativity of the basis via the sheaf axiom, the naturality clauses on U[Q], and the coefficient clause for C_E→C_Ω with x↦1⊗x. Edge cases checked: I=0, I=A, empty spectra or D=0, non-finite integral q, rank 0, and incomplete Ω. Batch-5 flags: lem-trf-henselian-smooth-algebra-lifting (the target of both zl flags) is generic henselian algebra, and def-trf-geometric-morphism (target of the component-cohomology flag) is a general definition; neither is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so all three are accepted. No SGA is cited, and nothing cited is dropped or merged. Two advisories, no faults: step 3 could also cite integral base change for integrality on affine opens, and the locality stmt_dep in the new node is slightly odd but harmless.
